title: The World's Tallest Wooden Tower Is Leaning | China Travel Expert
description:
For 970 years the Yingxian Wooden Pagoda in Shanxi — the Sakyamuni Pagoda of Fogong Temple, built in 1056 — rode out earthquake after earthquake. About 67 m of timber, raised with interlocking dougong brackets and mortise-and-tenon joints, not a single nail. The frame is built to move: the joints slip a little and burn off the shaking, so the tower sways instead of snapping.

So here's the twist — the thing bending it now isn't an earthquake. It's us. In the 1930s a 'repair' stripped out the mud in-fill walls and the diagonal braces that stiffened the second storey. After that, and the 1926 and 1948 wartime shelling, the frame started to drift: a column on the second floor now leans by as much as 57 cm. Experts drew up four rescue plans back in 2002 — and shelved every one of them while they argued over how to fix it without taking the tower apart.

★ Expert Tip: the upper floors have been closed to visitors for years, so plan to admire this one from the ground.

应县木塔屹立970年，抗住无数地震——真正让它倾斜的，是1930年代拆掉夹泥墙与斜撑的那次"维修"。二层一柱最大倾斜约57厘米；2002年起四套修缮方案全部搁置，上层已封闭。

• Built 1056 (Liao dynasty), world's tallest wooden pagoda, ~67 m, dougong + no nails, and its survival of repeated earthquakes: Wikipedia, "Pagoda of Fogong Temple" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pagoda_of_Fogong_Temple + Mi et al., "Analysis of the Residual Deformation of Yingxian Wood Pagoda," Advances in Civil Engineering (2020) https://structurae.net/en/literature/journal-article/analysis-of-the-residual-deformation-of-yingxian-wood-pagoda
